quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal quickly several times.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.explanation: When a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the accelerator. Do not brake hard. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You can turn right on red light if you are careful.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means right turns are prohibited.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Drive faster to protect your right-of-way.
Always stay in your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other road surfaces. They also thaw out later. This happens because bridges are exposed to cold air from above and below.

questions.question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly blocks traffic.
Yes, it is good defensive driving.
Yes, it is always safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly blocks traffic.
questions.explanation: Slow down when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive too slowly and block the normal flow of traffic, you may get a ticket.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what should you know?

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires do not grip well on loose gravel and dirt. You must slow down. It takes much longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop and start than small vehicles. If you stop suddenly in front of them, the driver may not be able to stop in time and a crash could happen.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Driving speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because drivers behind you may become frustrated and make unsafe moves to pass you. It is safest to drive with the flow of traffic and follow the speed limit.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.explanation: Never drive around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, wait until you can see clearly in both directions and confirm no trains are coming before crossing.

questions.question: What happens when you slow down to look at collisions or other unusual events?

options.text: It causes traffic congestion.
It prevents rear-end collisions.
It improves traffic flow.

questions.explanation: Avoid slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events. This is called "rubbernecking" and it causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: What can sudden wind gusts on highways do?

options.text: Generally affect only large vehicles.
Only create visibility problems.
Cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust into the roadway and can physically push a vehicle.

questions.question: When can you pass on the right shoulder of the road?

options.text: When the car in front of you is turning.
When the car in front of you is driving too slowly.
Never.

questions.explanation: Never drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle. You can only pass on the right when it is safe and legal to do so on the roadway.

questions.question: What type of drug is alcohol?

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows all body functions and nerve signals. It reduces inhibitions and makes it harder to concentrate and stay alert.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a parked position at a curb, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of traffic.
Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into any traffic, wait for a gap that is large enough for your vehicle to reach the same speed as other traffic.

questions.question: When entering a roadway from an alley, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the sidewalk.
Honk your horn.
The speed limit is 15 mph.

questions.explanation: When entering a road from an alley or driveway, you must stop before you reach the sidewalk.

questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed steady to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Put your car in neutral while driving through the water.

questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles to prevent skidding. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to get other drivers' attention.
Get out and wave down the next car that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your car if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your car if you can.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay in your car because the fast traffic on interstates makes it dangerous to stand or walk on the roadway.

questions.question: Which statement describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: They know other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
They expect no help and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers prepare for mistakes that other drivers might make.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in the rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: Slow down in rain to reduce hydroplaning risk. Driving too fast can make your tires lose contact with the road and make the car hard to control.

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Stop.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: The broken yellow line means you can pass. The solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.explanation: A triangle pointing down is always a yield sign. You must be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: A U-turn is not allowed:

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road with clear sight for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near a curve or hill. You may not see oncoming traffic or pedestrians, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: You can drive off the road to pass another vehicle:

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes going your direction.
Never.

questions.explanation: Never drive off the road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels and makes you lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels and makes you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on ice or snow can lock your front wheels and cause you to lose control. Drive slowly to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk straight after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are under the legal limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts your judgment. Good judgment is needed to react to traffic. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and cross carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Start slowing down when you see it.
